text: dsh-review 是面向 DSH 网页客户端的代码审阅侧栏插件。它通过 Host 端 workspaceReview 远程服务读取会话工作区，并在原生右侧栏或 dsh-better-sidebar 注册审阅页。用户可以按目录检查暂存、未暂存和未跟踪改动及行数差异，查看每轮会话操作、近期提交和文件内容，也可在启用编辑后保存文件。适合希望在 DSH 会话中直接追踪代码变更并浏览工作区文件的开发者。安装需要 DSH web profile 和工作区访问能力；不需要额外 API Key。

dsh-review adds a review panel to the DSH web sidebar. It reads the session workspace and shows uncommitted changes, edits by conversation round, commits, and files. Users can inspect diffs and optionally edit files. It requires the DSH web profile and workspace access; no API key is needed.
想在 DSH 网页侧栏里直接看工作区改了哪些文件。
有没有办法按目录查看暂存和未提交的代码差异？
我想知道 Agent 每一轮对话分别改了什么。
需要在 DSH 里浏览最近提交并查看某个文件的提交差异。
想从会话界面浏览工作区文件，必要时直接编辑保存。
I want to inspect my workspace changes and diffs inside the DSH web UI.
How can I review file changes grouped by conversation turn or commit?
dsh-review 的功能「未提交变更审阅」：在网页侧栏按目录展示暂存、未暂存和未跟踪文件及增删行数；选择文件可查看解析后的 unified diff，并显示分支状态和汇总。
dsh-review 的功能「按对话轮次查看改动」：从实时会话快照归并每轮工具结果涉及的文件和差异，按轮次展示增删内容，便于定位某轮 Agent 操作。
dsh-review 的功能「提交历史审阅」：列出最近提交，展开后查看该提交涉及的文件和逐文件差异；提交文件清单按需读取。
dsh-review 的功能「工作区文件浏览」：在侧栏列出工作区文件并读取所选文件内容，也提供明确开启后的文件编辑保存入口。

dsh-review README · dsh-review：An opencode-style **Review** panel for the [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) web GUI's right sidebar. One plugin owns both ends of its data path — a `git` service on the Host and a `review` tab in the browser — and shows the session workspace four ways:

dsh-review README · dsh-review：- **Uncommitted** — the working tree against `HEAD`, as a directory tree of every changed file, with per-file `+added`/`-removed`, the branch's grand total, and the selected file's unified diff in red/green.
- **Rounds** — what the agent changed in each conversation round, derived from the live conversation snapshot, shown with the same tree and the same diff body.
- **Commits** — the recent commit history, newest first; a commit expands to the tree of files it touched, with its own counts, and selecting a file shows that path's diff *within* that commit. Commit files are read lazily, only when a commit is opened.
- **Files** — a plain workspace browser: the tree of the workspace's files, **including git-ignored ones** such as `.env` (`git ls-files --cached --others` plus `--ignored`), with the heavy generated directories (`node_modules`, `__pycache__`, virtualenvs) left out; the selected file's content on the right, and an **opt-in editor** (off by default) for direct edits. It is a *file* browser, not a repository browser: a folder that is not a Git work tree is walked directly, so the tree is there with or without `git`. Folders start collapsed wit

dsh-review README · dsh-review：The look is a deliberate port of **opencode's** right-hand review panel (see [docs/REFERENCES.md](docs/REFERENCES.md)): 28px tree rows with a 6px radius and whole-row hover/selection, a rotating chevron, 12px names, **language-aware file-type icons** (Python, JS/TS, JSON, Markdown, … via the harness's own `FileTypeIcon`), an uppercase change letter in the theme's state colour, tabular-figure counts, and a segmented source switch.

dsh-review README · What it does：- **A directory tree, not a flat list.** Files group under folders, each folder row carries the totals for everything below it, and a chain of single-child directories is folded into one row (`src/client/`) — the same shape opencode's review pane uses. Root-level files sit beside the tree. A header toggle hides the per-folder aggregates when only the files matter.
- **A viewer escape hatch.** Every changed file has an **Open in a tab** action in its diff header, which opens the file in the sidebar's own file viewer (the native document preview, or `dsh-better-sidebar`'s editor) so it can be read without the diff decoration. The address is built by the harness's own grammar — every id and path segment encoded — so a name holding a space, `#`, `?` or `%` opens *that* file and not a truncated path nothing can claim. When the panel's own opener is switched off (better-sidebar's `editor` tab is disabled in the side card settings, which its `openTab` refuses with a console warning only), the column's `openResource` is used instead, and if neither can serve the click the button is disabled with the reason on screen rather than silently doing nothing.

dsh-review README · Install：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-review
dsh-review README · or, from a checkout:：dsh plugin --profile web add /path/to/dsh-review

dsh-review README · or straight from this repository:：dsh plugin --profile web add github:plae-tljg/dsh-review
```

The built artifacts are committed under `lib/`, so a git install needs no build step. Restart the harness (`dsweb`), then open the right panel's **+** menu → **审阅**. The tab registers both in the native right sidebar and in [`dsh-better-sidebar`](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/DSH-better-sidebar) when that plugin is present.

dsh-review README · or straight from this repository:：For development against a checkout, symlink the package into a profile's `node_modules` (which keeps rebuilds instant) and rebuild only the browser half:sh
ln -sfn /path/to/dsh-review ~/.dsh/profiles/web/node_modules/dsh-review
node build/build.mjs
```

A page refresh is enough to pick up a client rebuild; the Host half needs a restart.

dsh-review README · Build：```sh
node build/build.mjs
```

The build resolves `esbuild` and `zod` from a harness checkout rather than from this package, because the `clientBundle` tsdown preset that emits the browser format lives inside the repository and is not published. Override the checkout with `DSH_CHECKOUT=/path/to/deepseek-harness`.

Two artifacts come out:

dsh-review README · Build：| Artifact | Plane | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `lib/index.js` | Host (Node) | ESM; every `@deepseek-ai/*` specifier external, `zod` bundled |
| `lib/client.js` | Browser | the shell's lazy-CJS factory, `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({ id, factory })`, with the compiled CSS inlined and injected on materialization |
| `lib/typert.host.js` | Host | the hand-maintained Typert wire manifest |

dsh-review README · Test：`tests/parse.test.mjs` runs the Host parsers over recorded `git` output; `tests/host-diff.test.mjs` pins which paths take the null-device route and which must not; `tests/host-files.test.mjs` and `tests/host-commits.test.mjs` drive the Files and commit reads against throwaway repositories (and a plain directory outside Git); `tests/rounds.test.mjs` drives the round derivation against a hand-built snapshot; `tests/face.test.mjs` covers the deadline-guarded reads and the refresh that drops a stale body; `tests/file-address.test.mjs` holds the address builder to the harness's own expectations; `tests/client-wiring.test.mjs` loads `lib/client.js` in a VM and asserts every registration, including which opener the panel resolves; `tests/render.test.mjs` renders the tree and both sources through `react-dom/server`.

dsh-review README · Test：`npm test` builds first, so it needs `DSH_CHECKOUT` pointed at a harness checkout (the default is the author's path, not yours). A fresh clone also has no `node_modules`: the harness-owned specifiers (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-typert-protocol` for the Host tests, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-store` for the render tests) must resolve from the clone, while React and React DOM come from the active web profile. Link or install those rows, and put the checkout's `react`/`scheduler` on `NODE_PATH` if the profile's copies are missing:

dsh-review README · Test：```sh
H=/path/to/deepseek-harness
mkdir -p node_modules/@deepseek-ai
ln -sfn $H/packages/typert/protocol   node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh-typert-protocol
ln -sfn $H/packages/client/store      node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-store

dsh-review README · Architecture：```
src/index.js               Host plugin entry: re-exports the service
src/host/review.js         WorkspaceReview — the `workspaceReview` Remote service (git reads, plus the Files walk)
src/host/unified.js        unified-diff, --numstat, status and tree parsers
src/client/index.js        Browser entry: mount, native, and panel children

dsh-review README · Architecture：**Three client children, not one.** Cordis guards namespace access, and one absent optional service must not stall the rest: the *mount* child mounts the Remote contribution and registers dictionaries, the *ui* child registers the native `sidebar.right.pane.tab`, and the *panel* child registers into `dsh-better-sidebar` — injecting `betterSidebar` so it waits for that service instead of racing it with `ctx.get`.

dsh-review README · Architecture：**No core assembly is touched.** A Remote namespace normally has to be value-imported and mounted by `packages/api/remotes`; this plugin instead calls `ctx.remote.$mount()` itself, the documented escape hatch for a contribution that does not use a generated artifact.

dsh-review README · Configuration：Deployment caps are the service's Cordis config:

```yaml
- id: review
  name: 'dsh-review'
  config:
    maxDiffBytes: 2097152     # largest patch that crosses the wire; larger arrives cut

dsh-review README · Known limitations：- **Uncommitted list is memory-only and unrefreshed.** It reads when the tab mounts and when you press ⟳; there is no filesystem watch. The Rounds view follows the conversation live. A ⟳ re-reads the open diff body, so a file that changed on disk is shown as it is *now*, never as the patch the old report produced.
- **Code Mode (`run_code`) nested edits** are derived from the snapshot; the Host-side before/after recorder from the reference plugin is not ported, so an edge case that does not survive into the snapshot is not recovered.
- **Desktop split only.** The list and the diff sit side by side above 520px and stack below it; there is no draggable divider.
- **No word-level highlighting** and **no line comments** (opencode's inline-comment affordance is not ported).
- **The Files editor is a plain textarea** (no syntax highlighting; the browser's own undo applies). Binary and truncation-capped files are read-only.
